title: Self-Preservation in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12602v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Continual learning (CL) seeks to adapt pretrained models while preserving prior capabilities. Yet the tasks supplied for preservation cover only part of what a model knows, while forgetting can extend beyond them. Recent work shows that language models can supplement this limited evidence by generating useful replay without access to their original training data. This raises a question about self-preservation: can a model help choose preservation targets that protect its own capabilities more broadly? To study this question, we organize task descriptions and their examples into Task Banks, whose entries can be selected and combined to guide replay generation by a frozen model. Continual instruction tuning with Qwen models of varying sizes yields three findings. translated_title: 语言模型中的自我保存
translated_abstract: 持续学习旨在让预训练模型在适应新任务的同时保留原有能力。然而，用于保留的任务仅覆盖了模型所掌握知识的一部分，而遗忘的范围可能会超出这些任务。近期研究表明，语言模型可以在无法访问其原始训练数据的情况下，通过生成有用的重放样本（replay）来补充这些有限的证据。这引出了一个关于“自我保存”的问题：模型能否帮助选择保留目标，从而更广泛地保护自身的能力？为了研究这一问题，我们将任务描述及其示例组织成任务库，其条目可以被选择和组合，用以指导冻结模型的重放数据生成。使用不同规模的Qwen模型进行持续指令微调得出了三个发现。首先，新任务和学习率决定了哪些先前能力会发生退化，而跟踪之前回答正确的样本可以揭示平均准确率所掩盖的能力损失。其次，……
tldr: 该论文提出将任务描述及示例组织成任务库，让语言模型自行选择保留目标并生成重放数据，从而在持续学习中更广泛地保护自身原有能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes organizing task descriptions and examples into Task Banks, enabling language models to select preservation targets and generate replay data to more broadly protect their own capabilities during continual learning.
